title: Wallage / Old Westbury
summary: Wallage is a historical name associated with the Westbury settlement in North Hempstead. Later place histories consistently connect the older locality with the area now known as Old Westbury.
address_label: Old Westbury, Nassau County, NY (representative point)
map_geometry_source: Representative civic point in Old Westbury, supported by Tooker's North Hempstead/Westbury citation and later place histories.
why_this_matters: Wallage preserves an older layer beneath the names Woodedge, Westbury, and Old Westbury. Mapping the name broadly makes that sequence visible while acknowledging the disagreement in older printed sources.
introduction_content: Tooker's heading is Wallage, not Wallace. He cited one source calling it a name for Woodbury and another describing the North Hempstead settlement called Westbury. Additional Long Island histories place Wallage at the earlier Westbury or Old Westbury locality.
history_content: The official Village of Old Westbury history identifies this as the early settlement landscape north of Jericho Turnpike, first called Woodedge and later Westbury. Read with Tooker's North Hempstead citation and other historical mentions of Wallage, Old Westbury is the most responsible broad modern placement.
translation_content: Tooker tentatively compared Wallage with words for a ditch, hole, cave, hollow, or excavation. That comparison remains a historical suggestion rather than a confirmed modern-language translation.
preservation_content: This review record preserves the reference while leaving the location unresolved.
whereintheworld_content: The marker is a representative point at Old Westbury Village Hall. It identifies the broader Old Westbury locality and does not claim an exact historic tract boundary.
